newsitem.title: UK: OPEC, non-OPEC divide outdated - PdVSA's Guisti.
newsitem.headline: OPEC, non-OPEC divide outdated - PdVSA's Guisti.

text.p: The president of Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) said on Tuesday that traditional divisions between oil producers and consumers and between OPEC and non-OPEC producers were outdated.

"If we can make sure we can widen the dialogue between producers and consumers... and abandon the conventional wisdom of quotas, OPEC and non-OPEC...in the process we will find new ways of doing business today," Luis Guisti told the annual conference of the Centre for Global Energy Studies in London.

He said the energy market was a "complex mosaic" which would have to abandon short-sighted practices of the past if it was to meet the challenge of rising population growth and the inherent increase in demand for oil.

Guisti said oil world demand could rise to between 87 and 92 million barrels per day (bpd) by the year 2007 from a current level of 72 million bpd. He said PdVSA's commitment to an integrated oil industry could also provide a model for others to follow he said.
Guisti forecast the price volatility seen in 1996 and early 1997 was set to continue given a greater reliance on short-haul crude and a widely followed policy of low stocks.

"We believe there are indications that some of the new practices of low stocks and greater reliance on short-haul crude are here to stay. We will probably see more (price) volatility .... and regionalisation as a trend. It will be dictated by economics," Giusti told the conference.
